relationshipToReleaseCapabilities: ADDITIVE. GET /release/capabilities serves RELEASE_CAPABILITIES_R8_3.3 (asOf 2026-08-26) with a four-state vocabulary (ENABLED / LIMITED / DISABLED / EXPERIMENTAL_INTERNAL). That registry is the SERVER's statement about itself and is not replaced. This registry is the PRODUCT's statement about what v1 ships, in the five-state vocabulary NEW3 was asked for, and every row names the runtime row it derives from. Where the two disagree, the runtime registry wins on fact and this one wins on shipping decision.

backend.observedVia: GET /version on the live local backend

stateVocabulary.ENABLED_V1: Ships in v1, to every user, with the stated coverage and the stated uncertainty rendered.
stateVocabulary.INTERNAL_EXPERIMENTAL: Runs, is measured, is never reachable by a user in v1. No public surface, no marketing claim.
stateVocabulary.DISABLED_NOT_READY: The gap is OURS — code, coverage, or an unmeasured property. Closing it is our work.
stateVocabulary.DISABLED_EXTERNAL_BLOCK: The gap is NOT ours — an authorization, a credential, a registrar's answer. No amount of our work closes it.
stateVocabulary.POST_V1: Deliberately out of v1 scope. Not a gap.

minimumBackendVersionMeaning: The lowest `contract` integer (GET /version) at which a client may rely on this capability's response shape. Contract 1 is the only version that exists; a capability marked 2 is one whose shape is expected to change and which a v1 client must not depend on.

capabilities.coverageDefinition: judgments carrying a neutral citation / 18,758,460 judgments = 1,389,048 = 7.4049%. This is NOT the hit rate: a citation the advocate types is a citation that was printed, and the population of printed citations is not the population of judgments. The honest statement is 'every neutral citation we hold resolves', never 'we resolve every citation'.
capabilities.freshnessDefinition: Bounded by ingest, not by an index. A judgment is searchable by its citation from the moment its row exists. GET /corpus/freshness/object publishedAt 2026-08-29T14:40:46.848Z: latestLocalDecisionDate 2026-08-28, sourceLagDays 0.
capabilities.uncertaintyRendered: UNIQUE_UNCONFIRMED_STALE_INDEX where any of three freshness checks implicate the citation; shared-neutral identity returns every candidate and never a rank-1 pin.

capabilities.coverageDefinition: 18,758,433 / 18,758,460 = 99.99986% of held judgments carry a CNR. DENOMINATOR WARNING: this is coverage over judgments WE HOLD, and it is not a statement about eCourts. The CNR was backfilled from the same AWS High Court metadata the judgment came from. A CNR lookup answers 'do we hold this judgment', never 'what is happening in this case'.
capabilities.freshnessDefinition: Same as the judgment row. There is no separate CNR refresh and none is claimed.
capabilities.uncertaintyRendered: None needed — a CNR either resolves to a held judgment or does not.

capabilities.dataDependency: judgments.case_number, printed exactly as the court printed it
capabilities.coverageDefinition: 18,758,457 / 18,758,460 = 99.99998%. Case numbers are NOT unique across courts, so this arm returns candidates and the response says how many.
capabilities.uncertaintyRendered: Candidate list, never a pin, when more than one court printed the same number.

capabilities.coverageDefinition: Every held judgment has a title. The capability is bounded by QUERY SHAPE, not by coverage: a full or near-full title resolves at rank 1; a party name alone does not.

capabilities.runtimeRow: no dedicated row — it falls through to the lexical arm
capabilities.coverageDefinition: MEASURED ZERO on the two probes run. 'SANJAY KUMAR MISHRA @ SANJAY MISHRA' returns 0 results with degraded=[sparse_unbounded] and emptyBecause=query_too_broad_to_rank at rarestDf 0.0654. 'SATENDER KUMAR ANTIL' — an authority we hold and the most-cited node in the sampled citation graph, 7,418 inbound edges — returns 0 with degraded=[sparse_timeout] at rarestDf 0.0055.
capabilities.whyNotReady: The party-name path exists in retrieve.ts (rarestToken + trigram narrowing) but the request never reaches it: the query is classified as ordinary text and admitted or refused by the corpus-wide document-frequency gate first. This is the highest-value single gap in v1 search — an advocate names a case by its parties, not by its full cause title.

capabilities.coverageDefinition: 27 courts held. district and tribunal are reported as unpopulatedCourtCategories on EVERY search response — the filter exists, the data behind it does not, and the response says so rather than returning a silent empty.
capabilities.knownLimit: FILTERS DO NOT BOUND THE LEXICAL ADMISSION GATE. See capability search.filtered_broad_query.

capabilities.runtimeRow: no row — the behaviour is a refusal inside search.lexical
capabilities.coverageDefinition: MEASURED. 'bail' restricted to courts=[hc] over 2026-08-01..2026-08-29 — a window holding 45,660 judgments (measured) — is still refused with degraded=[sparse_unbounded], emptyBecause=query_too_broad_to_rank, rarestDf 0.2577. The same window with 'anticipatory bail cheque dishonour' returns 5 results in 103.6 ms.
capabilities.whyNotReady: READ FROM THE CODE, not inferred: services/api/src/search/retrieve.ts computes rarestDf from lexeme_document_frequency and refuses when rarestDf > SPARSE_MAX_RANKED_DOCUMENT_FREQUENCY (0.05, ~935,000 documents). `filters` is a parameter of that same function and is NOT consulted before the refusal. The bound is therefore corpus-wide while the query is not. An advocate who has already narrowed to one court and one month is told their query is too broad — which is the daily-loop case, and the one where narrowing is exactly what they did.

capabilities.coverageDefinition: full_text_tsv is GENERATED ALWAYS. Lexical coverage equals ingest coverage exactly, at every instant, with no backfill job and no lag. This is the ONLY coverage number in this registry that is 100% by construction rather than by measurement.
capabilities.freshnessDefinition: Identical to ingest. No separate index freshness exists.
capabilities.uncertaintyRendered: degraded[] carries sparse_timeout / sparse_unbounded / dense_timeout / pin_timeout; retrievalOutcome.state carries coverage_unknown; emptyBecause carries a reason and a remedy. A degraded search never renders as a complete one.

capabilities.coverageDefinition: A query over 500 characters is REFUSED with 400 and a message that says nothing was shortened. Verified: a 600-character query returns 400 with 'This search is longer than we can currently run safely'. Nothing is silently truncated.

Observed response carries: fullText, bodyText, textOrigin, paragraphs, numberedShare, dateQuality, dateQualityState, sourceUrl, plus all three citation fields and precedentialEffect / canAddToMatter / citableForUntouchedPropositions.
capabilities.freshnessDefinition: asOf is on the response. overruledStatus is read live at render and overruledStatusStored is carried beside it, so a stale stored value is visible rather than served.
capabilities.knownLimit: The reader refuses body-derived evidence for a judgment whose body text is convicted damaged, and says so as bodyText.evidenceWithheld. It does not render an empty page.

capabilities.coverageDefinition: TWO DIFFERENT NUMBERS, AND CONFLATING THEM WOULD BE THE WORST CLAIM IN THIS REGISTRY. (a) source_url present: 18,758,460 / 18,758,460 = 100.0000% — we can always say where the document came from. (b) RETAINED SOURCE ARTIFACT: official_source_artifact holds 14,210 rows against 18,758,460 judgments = 0.07575%, of which 655 are TEXT_AVAILABLE, 10,498 IMAGE_ONLY_OCR_PENDING and 3,057 have a null text_state. We retain the original bytes for well under a tenth of one percent of the corpus.

capabilities.bannedClaim: 'Verified from the retained official PDF' is FALSE for 99.92% of the corpus and must never appear on a judgment surface. 'Source: <court>, <url>' is true everywhere.

capabilities.coverageDefinition: FOUR NUMBERS, AND ONLY ONE OF THEM IS COVERAGE. judgment_citations holds 22,406,483 rows, of which 16,127,190 (71.98%) are BLANK SENTINELS — relationship 'cites' with an empty citation_text, meaning 'we looked and found nothing'. Real reference strings: 6,279,293. Resolved rows: 227,517 = 3.6233% of real reference strings. Distinct resolved edges: 200,761. Judgments with at least one resolved outgoing citation: 105,024 = 0.55987% of the corpus. Judgments cited at least once by a resolved edge: 35,153 = 0.18740%.

capabilities.bannedClaim: 'Every judgment has its citations mapped' would be arithmetically TRUE of judgment_citations row presence (18,758,460 of 18,758,460 judgments have at least one row) and completely false in meaning, because 71.98% of those rows are the blank sentinel. Citation coverage is defined on RESOLVED EDGES and on nothing else.
capabilities.contractGap: GET /judgments/:id/graph returns rootId, asOf, nodes, edges, totalNodes, returned, truncated. It does NOT declare that the graph is partial. `truncated` says 'this page is short', not 'this graph is 0.56% complete'. A partiality declaration is required before a graph reaches a user. See DATA_TRUST_CONTRACT.

capabilities.stateChangedBy: LCC R12, 30 August 2026, under the transformation this row's own `claimStatus` pre-authorised: "If the CAPTCHA blocker is withdrawn, this row becomes DISABLED_NOT_READY and NO OTHER ROW CHANGES." The blocker was withdrawn — it was invented by LCC and required by no document. CLAUDE.md §6a states the conditions on the bypass exhaustively and there are three, all mechanical and all already enforced. `whyExternallyBlocked` below is retained verbatim as the superseded claim; `whyNotReady` is the current one. monitoring.user_product is UNCHANGED and still fails gates 2, 3 and 4.
capabilities.whyNotReady: OURS, not a permission gap. The eCourts cause list serves no data until `cause_list_captcha_code` is satisfied, and satisfying it is an ENGINEERING problem under a written authorisation that expressly permits the bypass. What is outstanding is the request shape, the solver, an observation writer, and the two measurements monitoring waits on. AUTHORIZATION IS NOT REOPENED AND IS NOT A GATE.
capabilities.coverageDefinition: N/A. Retention is UNMEASURED for both High Court and district, and is recorded as UNMEASURED rather than estimated: every probe date meets the same wall, so twelve requests would buy twelve identical refusals.
capabilities.whyExternallyBlocked_SUPERSEDED_2026-08-: The first authorised eCourts request ever made under the registrar's grant returned the court's own answer: the cause list serves NO DATA until cause_list_captcha_code is satisfied. captchaBypassPermitted is true on the grant and the grant records NO operational basis — no credential, no whitelisted address, no exempt endpoint. Reading the image, transcribing the audio or exploiting the generator would each be inventing a security bypass. CAPTCHA_OPERATIONAL_BASIS = NONE_RECORDED. One sentence from the registrar closes this and nothing we build does.

At 17:29Z on 2026-08-29 LCC took the GIT_COMMIT lease with the task "R11b: correct the invented CAPTCHA blocker and complete the cause-list pipeline", and no correction had reached the bus (newest 1525) when this registry was written. If the CAPTCHA blocker is withdrawn, this row becomes DISABLED_NOT_READY and NO OTHER ROW CHANGES: monitoring.user_product still fails gates 2, 3 and 4.

capabilities.whyNotReady: FOUR separate gates, and the pilot passing closes only one. (1) the CAPTCHA basis; (2) an observation writer; (3) MEASURED capacity — the encoded limits are 2,000 ms minimum interval, 100/hour, 1,000/day, and naive per-matter-per-day polling caps the entire product at under ~1,000 monitored matters across all users, forever; (4) MEASURED retention. Pilot data existing is NOT one of the four.
capabilities.monetization: FORBIDDEN until (3) and (4) are measured. No SLA, no published polling frequency, no price.
